'''Nagarchal''' ({{IPA|nbg|naːɡɐrt͡ʃaːl}}) is an [[Unattested language|unattested]] extinct language of [[central India]], presumed to be [[Dravidian language|Dravidian]]. According to the 1971 census, there were 7,100 speakers of the language, but they have since apparently [[language shift|shifted]] to [[Hindi]] and [[Gondi language|Gondi]]. The Nagarchi people, who formerly spoke it, are found in the Balaghat, Chhindwara, Jabalpur, Mandla and Seoni districts of [[Madhya Pradesh]].<ref>{{e22|nbg|Nagarchal}}</ref> 

In an interview, Nagarchis said that their language was ''purani bhasha,'' which means "old language", that they shifted to Hindi and Gondi 15 to 20 years ago and they do not use the language even in the home domain at present. They said the language is very different from Hindi but close to Gondi implying it's likely a Gondic language. The researchers attempted to collect Nagarchi wordlists from many areas but this was not possible, as even elders were not able to provide wordlists in the Nagarchi language.<ref>{{Cite news |last=George |first=Symon |last2=Valte |first2=Thangmualian |last3=Mathai |first3=Eldose K. |title=A sociolinguistic survey among the Nagarchi community of central India |url=https://www.sil.org/resources/publications/entry/9044 |url-status=live |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20241201011600/https://www.sil.org/resources/publications/entry/9044 |archive-date=2024-12-01 |access-date=2026-02-16 |work=Journal of Language Survey Reports |language=en}}</ref>
